- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–4% upward bias for next 5–10 days.  
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 days’ sentiment-weighted price.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lagged sentiment trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean; apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1–3% of 30-day average from forecast if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
